terms.definition: Fine-tuning a pretrained model on tasks expressed as natural-language instructions so it becomes better at following instructions and generalizing to new tasks.
terms.example: Instruction tuning helped the model respond more reliably to unfamiliar tasks described in plain language.

terms.definition: Fine-tuning a pretrained model on labeled examples of desired inputs and outputs so its behavior better matches a target task or response style.
terms.example: The team used supervised fine-tuning on curated question-and-answer pairs before applying preference-based training.

terms.definition: A machine-learning approach in which an agent learns behavior by taking actions and receiving rewards or penalties based on their outcomes.
terms.example: The robot used reinforcement learning to improve its policy through repeated interaction with the environment.

terms.definition: A model trained to score or rank outputs according to preferences or desired behavior, providing a reward signal that can guide further model training.
terms.example: The reward model ranked two candidate responses so the training system could favor the one judged more helpful.

terms.definition: Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback, a training approach in which feedback or preferences generated by AI systems are used to create a reward signal for reinforcement learning.
terms.example: The experiment used RLAIF so an AI preference model, rather than only human raters, helped shape the assistant's behavior.

terms.definition: A model-compression and transfer technique in which a smaller or simpler model is trained to reproduce useful behavior or knowledge from a larger model or ensemble.
terms.example: The team used distillation to create a smaller model that retained much of the larger model's performance.

terms.definition: Reducing the numerical precision used to represent a model's weights or computations, usually to lower memory use and improve inference efficiency.
terms.example: Quantization reduced the model's memory footprint enough to run it on a smaller device.

terms.definition: Low-Rank Adaptation, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that keeps pretrained model weights fixed while training small low-rank matrices that modify the model's behavior.
terms.example: The team trained a LoRA adapter for the specialty domain instead of updating every parameter in the base model.

terms.definition: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning, a family of techniques that adapt pretrained models by training only a relatively small subset of parameters or added components instead of updating the full model.
terms.example: PEFT made it practical to maintain several specialized adaptations without storing a complete fine-tuned model for each task.

terms.definition: Using knowledge learned for one task, domain, or dataset to improve learning or performance on another related task or domain.
terms.example: Transfer learning let the team start from a pretrained model instead of training a new vision system from scratch.

terms.definition: A learning approach that creates training targets from the structure of unlabeled data itself, allowing models to learn useful representations without manually supplied labels for every example.
terms.example: The language model used self-supervised learning by predicting hidden or next tokens from raw text.

terms.definition: A machine-learning approach in which a model learns from examples paired with known labels or target outputs.
terms.example: The classifier used supervised learning from emails labeled as spam or not spam.

instruction-tuning.origin: Instruction tuning developed from transfer-learning and multitask fine-tuning work and became a prominent language-model technique when researchers fine-tuned pretrained models on collections of tasks expressed through natural-language instructions.

history.event: The FLAN paper described instruction tuning as fine-tuning a pretrained language model on many tasks verbalized with natural-language instructions and showed improved zero-shot performance.

sources.title: Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners

supervised-fine-tuning.origin: Supervised fine-tuning combines established supervised learning with fine-tuning of pretrained models. In modern language-model alignment pipelines, SFT commonly refers to training on curated demonstrations of desired responses before later preference or reinforcement-learning stages.

history.event: The InstructGPT paper described supervised fine-tuning on human-written demonstrations as the first stage of its alignment pipeline.

sources.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

reinforcement-learning.origin: Reinforcement learning is a long-established machine-learning field concerned with learning behavior through interaction and reward signals. It predates modern generative AI by decades.

history.event: Sutton and Barto's textbook consolidated reinforcement learning as a major framework for sequential decision making and learning from reward.

reward-model.origin: Reward models adapt preference learning to situations where the desired reward is not directly specified. In modern LLM alignment, they are trained from ranked outputs and used to supply a scalar reward for reinforcement learning.

history.event: InstructGPT trained a reward model on human rankings of model outputs and then optimized the language model against that learned reward signal.

sources.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

rlaif.origin: RLAIF, Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback, emerged as a named alternative or complement to reinforcement learning from human feedback in which AI-generated preferences help train the reward or preference signal.

firstKnownUse.note: Anthropic's Constitutional AI paper explicitly used the phrase ‘RL from AI Feedback’ and abbreviation RLAIF in a documented training method.

history.event: Anthropic's Constitutional AI paper described a reinforcement-learning phase using a preference model trained from AI-generated preferences and called the method RLAIF.

sources.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

distillation.origin: Model and knowledge distillation grew from earlier model-compression work. Hinton, Vinyals, and Dean's 2015 paper made knowledge distillation a widely recognized neural-network technique for transferring behavior from larger models or ensembles into smaller models.

history.event: Hinton, Vinyals, and Dean published ‘Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network,’ helping establish modern knowledge-distillation practice.

sources.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network

quantization.origin: Quantization is an older numerical-computing concept adapted to neural networks to reduce precision and resource requirements. In modern AI deployment it commonly reduces the bit width used for weights, activations, or both.

history.event: A survey of quantized neural networks documented quantization as an established approach for reducing model memory and computational requirements.

sources.title: A Survey on Methods and Theories of Quantized Neural Networks

lora.origin: Low-Rank Adaptation was introduced as LoRA by Hu and colleagues as a parameter-efficient way to adapt large pretrained language models while keeping the original weights frozen.

firstKnownUse.note: The original LoRA paper introduced the name Low-Rank Adaptation and the abbreviation LoRA.

history.event: The LoRA paper proposed freezing pretrained model weights while injecting trainable low-rank decomposition matrices into Transformer layers.

sources.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

peft.origin: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning is a broad family of adaptation methods that update only a small portion of model parameters or add small trainable components. It builds on earlier parameter-efficient transfer-learning methods such as adapters and later includes methods such as LoRA.

history.event: Houlsby and colleagues demonstrated parameter-efficient transfer learning with compact adapter modules while keeping the original pretrained network fixed.
LoRA provided a prominent low-rank parameter-efficient adaptation method for large language models.

sources.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

transfer-learning.origin: Transfer learning predates modern foundation models and describes reusing knowledge acquired in one learning setting to improve another. Pretraining followed by downstream adaptation is a major modern form of transfer learning.

history.event: Pan and Yang published a major survey formalizing transfer-learning settings and terminology across machine-learning research.

self-supervised-learning.origin: Self-supervised learning developed as a family of methods that derive supervisory signals from unlabeled data itself. It became central to modern representation learning and to pretraining methods such as masked-token and next-token prediction.

history.event: BERT used masked-language-model and next-sentence pretraining objectives that exemplify modern self-supervised learning from unlabeled text.

sources.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

supervised-learning.origin: Supervised learning is a foundational machine-learning paradigm that predates the current AI era. Models learn mappings from inputs to known labels or target outputs using labeled examples.
